title: LEAN-STA R: LEARNING TO INTERLEAVE THINKING AND PROVING
abstract: Lean-STaR is a framework for training language models to produce informal thoughts prior to each step of a proof, boosting theorem-proving capabilities. It uses retrospective ground-truth tactics to generate synthetic thoughts for training and applies expert iteration to fine-tune the model.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You don't just write down the solution - you think through the steps first. Chain-of-Thought is like this, but for computers. We're teaching language models to think before they prove, making them better at math.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: We use a powerful language model to generate thoughts based on ground-truth tactics. Then, we fine-tune the model to predict the next tactic after each thought. This process is repeated, with the model improving each time.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: Our model, Lean-STaR, achieves a pass rate of 34.8% on the miniF2F-test dataset, outperforming the base model (30.3%). With a stronger base model, InternLM2-Plus-7B, Lean-STaR reaches 46.3%.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Automated theorem proving can help discover errors in previous proofs and make new proofs more reliable. By combining informal thoughts with formal proofs, we're making progress towards more powerful and flexible theorem-proving systems.

config.title: Impact of Informal Thoughts on Theorem Proving

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Our approach introduces retrospective rationale generation and expert iteration to improve theorem-proving capabilities. These innovations enable language models to learn from their own thought processes and generate more accurate proofs.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: You can experiment with Lean-STaR using the InternLM2-Plus-7B model and the miniF2F-test dataset. Try fine-tuning the model with different datasets or adjusting the expert iteration parameters to see how it affects the pass rate.
